canonical_topic: Key inputs to a load forecast: consumer type, location, weather, calendar effects
definition: Load forecasts are built for bounded geographic areas (from neighborhoods up to multi-state regions), and the boundary chosen determines what mix of consumer types and what climate the model must account for; the author identifies consumer type, location, weather, and calendar effects as the most important forecasting factors.
core_idea: The geographic scope of a load forecast is what defines the 'spatial' part of spatial load forecasting, since it fixes both the consumer mix and the climate the model needs to represent.
key_points: Forecast areas can range in size from a neighborhood to a multi-state region.
The chosen boundary determines the consumer types present and the general climate of the region.
Consumer type, location, weather, and calendar effects are called out as among the most important factors in a load forecast.
relationships: Defines the spatial component referenced in 'spatial load forecasting'
